title: Replicating Agustini et al. (2026) with accuracylevel
text: article injects outliers clean regression shows proposed metrics degrade gradually, unlike RMSE/MAPE. mimic small simulated dataset. Conventional metrics (especially MAPE/RMSE) jump sharply. proposed Level-1 accuracy, evaluated fixed baseline threshold, moves far less:
code: set.seed(2026) n <- 200 x <- runif(n, 0, 100) y <- 1.5 * x + rnorm(n, 0, 3)            # clean response pred_clean <- 1.5 * x                    # model prediction  # 5% outliers injected into the response y_out <- y idx <- sample(n, size = 0.05 * n) y_out[idx] <- y_out[idx] + 80  baseline <- calculate_threshold(y, pred_clean, error_type = "ape", quartile = 3)  clean <- conventional_metrics(y, pred_clean) dirty <- conventional_metrics(y_out, pred_clean) rbind(clean = round(clean, 3), with_outliers = round(dirty, 3)) #>               R_squared  RMSE NRMSE   MAE   MAPE  SMAPE #> clean             0.996  2.77 0.040 2.220 11.495 10.756 #> with_outliers     0.853 17.99 0.248 6.078 14.044 14.654 al_clean <- accuracy_level(y,     pred_clean, threshold = baseline) al_dirty <- accuracy_level(y_out, pred_clean, threshold = baseline)  data.frame(   scenario = c("clean", "with_outliers"),   CSE_L1   = c(al_clean$metrics$CSE[1],  al_dirty$metrics$CSE[1]),   CAPE_L1  = c(al_clean$metrics$CAPE[1], al_dirty$metrics$CAPE[1]) ) #>        scenario CSE_L1 CAPE_L1 #> 1         clean   74.5    74.5 #> 2 with_outliers   71.5    71.0

title: Replicating Agustini et al. (2026) with accuracylevel
text: paper forecasts U.S. candy production (FRED IPG3113N). series public; load directly: self-contained demonstration simulate seasonal series compare two naive forecasts.
code: # Public source (not run during vignette build): # https://www.kaggle.com/code/goldens/candy-production-time-series-analysis candy <- read.csv("candy_production.csv") set.seed(1) m <- 48 trend <- seq(80, 120, length.out = m) season <- 10 * sin(2 * pi * (1:m) / 12) candy <- trend + season + rnorm(m, 0, 3)  fc_seasonal <- c(candy[1:12], candy[1:(m - 12)])    # seasonal-naive-like fc_mean     <- rep(mean(candy), m)                   # mean forecast  base_ts <- calculate_threshold(candy, fc_seasonal, error_type = "ape", quartile = 2)  data.frame(   model   = c("seasonal", "mean"),   CSE_L1  = c(accuracy_level(candy, fc_seasonal, threshold = base_ts)$metrics$CSE[1],               accuracy_level(candy, fc_mean,     threshold = base_ts)$metrics$CSE[1]) ) #>      model   CSE_L1 #> 1 seasonal 47.91667 #> 2     mean 43.75000

text: object class "accuracy_level" elements: metrics (data frame accuracy percentages level metric type), mean_errors (data frame mean errors per level), threshold (primary threshold object used), thresholds_all (per-error-type threshold objects), n_obs (number observations), counts (count observations level).

title: Compute Accuracy-Level Metrics — accuracy_level
text: accuracy-level method introduces four metrics: CSE (Counted Squared Error) Proportion observations within squared error threshold levels. CAE (Counted Absolute Error) Proportion observations within absolute error threshold levels. CAPE (Counted Absolute Percentage Error) Proportion observations within absolute percentage error threshold levels. SCAPE (Symmetric Counted Absolute Percentage Error) Proportion observations within symmetric absolute percentage error threshold levels. metric, four accuracy levels defined: Level 1: \(\varepsilon < T\) (highest accuracy) Level 2: \(T \le \varepsilon < 2T\) Level 3: \(2T \le \varepsilon < 5T\) Level 4: \(\varepsilon \ge 5T\) (lowest accuracy) T base threshold determined baseline model's error distribution.  Crucially, thresholds CSE, CAE, CAPE, SCAPE derived quartile baseline model's SE, AE, APE, sAPE respectively (Figure 2 paper). Edge cases handled follows: observations non-finite error (example APE actual zero, sAPE actual predicted zero) assigned Level 4. baseline threshold T equals zero (perfectly fitting baseline), machine-epsilon boundary used exact-zero errors fall Level 1.

title: Compute Accuracy-Level Metrics — accuracy_level
code: # ---- Paper Table 4: Simple case ---- actual <- c(7, 6.03, 2.02, 5.1, 9, 1, 3, 4.38, 1, 8.07) m1 <- c(6.05, 5.02, 1.32, 5.15, 8, 2.2, 2.7, 3.48, 1, 7.56) m3 <- c(7.01, 6.04, 2.09, 5.11, 9.01, 5.1, 3.01, 4.39, 1, 8.1)  # Model 1 as baseline, Q2 thresh <- calculate_threshold(actual, m1, quartile = 2)  # Evaluate Model 3 (paper expects 90% at L1) result <- accuracy_level(actual, m3, threshold = thresh) print(result) #> Accuracy-Level Metrics #> ====================== #> Observations: 10  #> Threshold quartile: Q2 #> Multipliers: 2, 5  #>  #> Accuracy by Level (%): #>  Level CSE CAE CAPE SCAPE #>     L1  90  90   90    90 #>     L2   0   0    0     0 #>     L3   0   0    0     0 #>     L4  10  10   10    10 #>  #> Interpretation: #>   L1: Highest accuracy (error < T) #>   L4: Lowest accuracy  (error >= 5T) #>   Higher L1 values indicate better model performance.

what: Calculate Error Thresholds from a Baseline Model — calculate_threshold
title: Calculate Error Thresholds from a Baseline Model — calculate_threshold
text: Calculate error threshold levels based baseline model's error distribution. threshold determined using quartiles specified error type, following procedure Figure 2 Agustini et al. (2026). Quartiles computed using inverse empirical CDF (R's type = 1), consistent paper.

title: Calculate Error Thresholds from a Baseline Model — calculate_threshold
code: calculate_threshold(   actual,   predicted,   error_type = c("ape", "sape", "se", "ae"),   quartile = 2,   multipliers = c(2, 5) )

title: Calculate Error Thresholds from a Baseline Model — calculate_threshold
text: actual Numeric vector actual (observed) values baseline model. predicted Numeric vector predicted values baseline model. error_type Character string specifying error type used select quartile. One "ape" (default, absolute percentage error), "sape" (symmetric APE), "se" (squared error), "ae" (absolute error). quartile Integer (1, 2, 3) specifying quartile use. Default 2 (median). recommended approach paper select quartile APE value close 0.1 (10 percent error). multipliers Numeric vector length 2 specifying multipliers level boundaries. Default c(2, 5), creating levels L1: error < T, L2: T <= error < 2T, L3: 2T <= error < 5T, L4: error >= 5T.

title: Calculate Error Thresholds from a Baseline Model — calculate_threshold
text: list class "al_threshold" elements: threshold (base threshold value T), levels (list L1–L4 boundary pairs), error_type (error type used), quartile (quartile used), multipliers (multiplier values), baseline_quartiles (named list selected quartile value every error type: se, ae, ape, sape – key element lets accuracy_level derive thresholds four metrics single baseline model).

title: Calculate Error Thresholds from a Baseline Model — calculate_threshold
text: Agustini, M., Fithriasari, K., & Prastyo, D.D. (2026). accuracy-level method robust evaluation predictive analytics. Decision Analytics Journal, 18, 100661. doi:10.1016/j.dajour.2025.100661

title: Calculate Error Thresholds from a Baseline Model — calculate_threshold
code: # --- Paper Table 4: simple case, Model 1 as baseline --- actual  <- c(7, 6.03, 2.02, 5.1, 9, 1, 3, 4.38, 1, 8.07) model1  <- c(6.05, 5.02, 1.32, 5.15, 8, 2.2, 2.7, 3.48, 1, 7.56)  # Q2 of APE ~ 0.1111, close to the target 0.10 thresh <- calculate_threshold(actual, model1, quartile = 2) print(thresh) #> Accuracy-Level Threshold #> ======================== #> Error type: ape  #> Quartile: Q2 #> Base threshold (T): 0.1111  #> Multipliers: 2, 5  #>  #> Level Boundaries (ape): #>   L1: error < 0.1111  #>   L2: 0.1111 <= error < 0.2222  #>   L3: 0.2222 <= error < 0.5556  #>   L4: error >= 0.5556  #>  #> Baseline Q2 for all error types: #>   SE:   0.49  #>   AE:   0.7  #>   APE:  0.1111  #>   sAPE: 0.1176   # Stricter thresholds via Q1 thresh_q1 <- calculate_threshold(actual, model1, quartile = 1)

text: Initial release. package implements accuracy-level evaluation metrics Agustini, Fithriasari, Prastyo (2026) doi:10.1016/j.dajour.2025.100661.

title: accuracylevel 0.1.0
text: Four accuracy-level metrics 0-100% scale: Counted Squared Error (cse()), Counted Absolute Error (cae()), Counted Absolute Percentage Error (cape()), Symmetric Counted Absolute Percentage Error (scape()), plus accuracy_level() four . Baseline threshold tools: calculate_threshold() auto_threshold(), quartiles computed inverse empirical CDF (type = 1) match paper. compare_models() implements Figure 3 model-selection rule: Level-1 accuracy first, ties broken level’s mean error (lower better) advancing next level. comparison table reports accuracy mean error per level. Conventional robust benchmarks: conventional_metrics() (R-squared, RMSE, NRMSE, MAE, MAPE, SMAPE), robust_metrics() (MedAE, trimmed MSE, Huber loss, quantile loss), compare_all_metrics(). Framework integration: caret_summary() / caret_summary_extended() / caret_single_metric() caret; cse_l1(), cae_l1(), cape_l1(), scape_l1(), accuracy_level_metrics(), al_metric_set() tidymodels/yardstick; al_forecast_accuracy(), al_compare_forecasts(), al_extended_accuracy(), al_tsCV() forecast. vignette("replication") reproduces simple-case (Table 4-6), regression--outlier, time-series results, plus caret/tidymodels/forecast integrations. imputation case study omitted relies confidential firm-level microdata BPS-Statistics Indonesia redistributed.

title: accuracylevel 0.1.0
text: Perfect predictions (actual == predicted) give zero baseline threshold; machine-epsilon boundary used exact-zero errors assigned Level 1. Non-finite per-observation errors (example absolute percentage error actual value zero) assigned Level 4. pre-computed threshold object supplied accuracy_level(), four per-error-type thresholds derive stored baseline quartiles, every model evaluated baseline (Figure 2 paper).
